summary: S7 module is one of the strongest OT modules. It reaches T2 concretely via read_var_ok (FC 0x04 M0.0 succeeds → proof PUT/GET is exploitable) and via the CVE-2016-9159 legacy password readout (SZL 0x0132 index 3 → 8-byte obfuscated password + deobfuscation → cleartext hint). CVE fingerprint pipeline maps MLFB order code to CVE-2015-2177/CVE-2016-9159/CVE-2020-15782/CVE-2022-38465. Biggest gap: does not chain the deobfuscated password back into an authenticated snap7 session, and never actually attempts FC 0x29 STOP even opt-in.

findings.title_pattern: Siemens S7 PLC reachable on scanned network
findings.tier_evidence: COTP CR/CC handshake with TSAP walk is a positive S7-family fingerprint, not a bare port-open guess.
findings.promotion_notes: Segmentation stance — cannot promote without pivoting off the same T1 evidence.
findings.tester_next_step: plcscan -p 102 <ip>; snap7-client -h <ip> -c connect -R 0 -S 2 (rack 0 slot 2 = classic S7-300/400 CPU location).

findings.title_pattern: S7 COTP layer reachable, S7COMM setup rejected
findings.tier_evidence: COTP-CC but no S7 setup — protocol layer reachable, no vuln evidence.
findings.promotion_notes: Try alternate TSAPs (0x4C01, 0x4C02 for S7-1500 basic panel), and probe port 102 for RUGGEDCOM/OMSA disguised iso-tsap listeners.
findings.tester_next_step: for tsap in 0100 0200 0201 0300 4c01 4c02 1000; do python -c "import snap7; c=snap7.client.Client(); c.set_connection_params('<ip>',0x0100,int('$tsap',16)); c.connect_tsap()"; done

findings.tier_evidence: Protocol byte 0x72 identifies S7COMM-PLUS — fingerprint only.
findings.promotion_notes: Parse the OPN/S7CommPlus fields more deeply to extract PLC serial / hardware version; correlate against CVE-2020-15782 firmware bands.
findings.tester_next_step: snap7-plus-cli connect <ip>; check firmware via TIA Portal Online-Diagnostics; correlate with SSA-434534 and SSA-568427.

findings.tier_evidence: Setup Communication ACK with parameter 0xF0 is deterministic evidence classic S7COMM is spoken.
TSAP list is rack/slot layout — fingerprint only.
findings.tester_next_step: Try each confirmed TSAP with snap7-client set_connection_params — one may reach a CP343-1/CP443-1 with different protection level than the CPU.

findings.title_pattern: S7 CPU identity disclosed (order code + firmware)
findings.tier_evidence: SZL 0x0011 read — protocol-exposed fingerprint feeding CVE map.
findings.promotion_notes: Already partly promoted via cve_matches; keep the MLFB itself informational and rely on s7_firmware_cve for the T1 evidence.
findings.tester_next_step: MLFB decoded — search Siemens ProductCERT + siemens.com/cert-services for MLFB prefix; consult CVE-2015-2177/CVE-2016-9159 for 6ES73* CPUs.

findings.tier_evidence: SZL 0x001C free-text — high info-leak value but not proof of vuln.
findings.promotion_notes: Info-leak is the whole finding — feed serial into cross-scan correlation via known_ot_assets.
findings.tester_next_step: Record plant_designation / location — often names the physical process/site. Correlate serial against vendor RMA / engineering-station project files if reachable.

findings.title_pattern: S7 PUT/GET communication enabled — unauthenticated memory read/write
findings.tier_evidence: SZL 0x0131 index 3 record_seen — deterministic proof PUT/GET is enabled.
findings.promotion_notes: Chain into s7_read_var_ok result: if read succeeded on M0.0, that IS the T2 proof.
findings.tester_next_step: snap7-client -h <ip> -c getvar -a M -s 0 -n 1; then enumerate DBs: snap7-client -c listblocks; snap7-client -c getvar -a DB -d 1 -s 0 -n 16 — dump plant recipes/setpoints without auth.

findings.tier_evidence: FC 0x04 return_code 0xFF is a concrete unauthenticated 1-byte read of a real CPU memory area — proof of exploit, not stance.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 would be full DB dump / block upload + interpretation. Recce deliberately stops at 1 byte to avoid noise; a --s7-dump mode could enumerate DBs and pull first N bytes of each.
findings.tester_next_step: snap7-client -h <ip> -c getvar -a DB -d <n> -s 0 -n 256 for each DB from the block list; snap7-client -h <ip> -c dbget -d 1 (full DB1 dump) — expect process setpoints, recipes, alarms.

findings.tier_evidence: SZL 0x0232 index 4 exposes the CPU protection level byte deterministically.
findings.promotion_notes: Level 1 means STOP/START/block upload accepted without password — send FC 0x29 STOP (behind --s7-stop) for T2. Destructive.
findings.tester_next_step: snap7-client -h <ip> -c szl -i 0x0232 -x 4; if level=1, DO NOT run stop against production. Test-cell prove: snap7-client -h <ip> -c stop then snap7-client -c start.

findings.tier_evidence: SZL 0x0132 index 3 returns the CPU password blob AND the module deobfuscates it in _deobfuscate_s7_password → cleartext CPU credential recovered without auth. That IS initial access to the CPU.
findings.promotion_notes: T4 chain: use recovered password to open an authenticated snap7 session, dump every DB, upload OBs (function 0x1B), then rewrite OB1 (T4 = full PLC compromise).
findings.tester_next_step: Use the leg['cleartext_guess'] password: snap7-client -h <ip> -c connect --password '<CLEARTEXT>'; then snap7-client -c szl -i 0x0132; dump every OB with snap7-client -c blockget -t OB -n <num>; NEVER write OBs against production.

findings.title_pattern: S7 CPU STOP/START function reachable — process DoS possible
findings.tier_evidence: Emitted whenever s7_stack is confirmed — proves protocol reachability of FC 0x29, not that STOP itself would succeed.
findings.promotion_notes: Only real proof is to send FC 0x29 STOP under --s7-stop; destructive on production, safe in test cell.
findings.tester_next_step: TEST-CELL ONLY: snap7-client -h <ip> -c stop; verify SF LED on CPU face; snap7-client -c start to recover. Never on production.

findings.title_pattern: S7 block list enumerated (OB/FB/FC/DB inventory disclosed)
findings.tier_evidence: UserData 0x0D reply with 4-byte records is deterministic block inventory — real program structure leak.
findings.promotion_notes: Enumerate specific DB numbers via block-upload (function 0x1B, UD subfn 0x1F); paired with put_get_enabled this is full logic exfil.
findings.tester_next_step: For each DB in blocks: snap7-client -h <ip> -c blockget -t DB -n <num>; write raw to disk and disassemble with plctool/snap7 to recover engineering IP.

findings.tier_evidence: MLFB prefix positively identifies family — deterministic CVE-family match; firmware band still needs confirmation.
findings.promotion_notes: Add firmware-band verification via SZL 0x0011 ausbg2 major/minor comparison against the CVE's patched-in-firmware release; only emit CVE tag when band matches, else CWE-1395 generic.
findings.tester_next_step: Compare fw_version to Siemens ProductCERT SSA-***; for CVE-2016-9159 confirm password readout worked; for CVE-2020-15782 use TIA Portal / snap7-plus PoC (private) against S7-1200 <V4.5.
